original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: One boundary implication of the inherited H2/K interface, tested exactly: can a common-frame helper entrance (#1253's 366 classes, all 4,954 supports, plus source donors) be compensated after the scatter instead of by a frame-0 prefix? Census on the selected PR589 word and the four merged star words (PR1062/1122/1188/1208), in a sound necessary class (LC-fav), the carrier-checked class A6 and A6 with storage relays (A6R).
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a replacement H2/K interface and a falsification on dirty inputs or chronological cuts. Rather than proposing a new contract, this narrows the late-compensation relaxation of the zero-start rule that #1128 (PROOF section 4) and #1179 leave open by name, to compensation after the scatter on fixed A and scatter, one entrance at a time.
bottleneck_link: Scoped negative result on the nonbinding bit side; no kappa. Moving the zero-start rule's compensation after the scatter admits no new entrance in the carrier-checked class A6 and, in the sound class LC-fav, only one open triple. Reason: every dirt-only space W_t is a coordinate subspace of at most 5 helpers (4 in A6), so only 98 (47) of 18,085 K incidences can be repaired late. A positive entrance would only save the pivot's first climb (-H1), which width-8 hosting cancels (#1179, #1253).
stop_rule: Stop once every support of #1253's closure and every enumerated source donor is decided in LC-fav and A6 on all five words (support verdicts by two engines, donors and the relaxation by engine 1), the only LC-fav survivor is classified under A6R, and controls confirm both directions; report an A6R-only survivor as an open handoff.
evidence: RESULT.json (identical on all five words): 4,954 supports. LC-fav admits only the #1179 kernel pair 444+470 (T empty) and the triple 444+470+578 (T = 8 targets); no single helper, no new pair, 0 of 5,212 enumerated (5,059 placeable) source donors. A6 admits only the kernel pair. Relaxation: one nonzero class (frame 79's line) with kernel {444+470, 578} (LC-fav) and {444+470} (A6), containing every admission. Every W_t is a coordinate subspace, dim <= 5 (LC-fav) and <= 4 (A6); covered K incidences 98 and 47 of 18,085. Triple: A6 covers 150 and 197; A6R(T only) 150, 153, 192, 197; A6R all 8, so it is OPEN. Engine 2 agrees on K, the closure (= #1253's certificate), every W_t and every support verdict. Controls: synthetic word admits 444+470 late at target 150 and its witness replays (and fails without its late reads; it equals #1179's entrance after B); K-bit flip and a relaxed carrier frame flip verdicts; flipped byte rejected; C reduces to the end of B. 20 tests pass.
author: Sagar Thakrar (thakrarsagar)
ai_assistance: Substantial: Claude (Anthropic) via Claude Code. Parallel read-only scout and judge subagents selected the question (both judges ranked it first); reader subagents and a synthesizer audited the scout's criterion (finding the triple the scout missed and the carrier gap in its strict class) and specified the classes; both engines, the proof note and the controls were then written fresh. A post-PR adversarial review corrected the witness description, the scope of the open triple, the citations and the controls (second commit).

open_questions.question: Can the triple 444+470+578 be realised in LC-fav?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only support surviving the sound test; within A6R its 8 targets are covered only through relays outside T, while a rewritten B reading 470 and source 77 directly is not excluded.
open_questions.first_step: Record the reads A6R uses per target, build a candidate (relays first, then a rewritten B reading 77 directly) and test it with wlib.replay and #1179's literal stream checks.
open_questions.blocked_by: Restoring the relay targets, or a legal rewritten B.

open_questions.question: Do two or more simultaneous entrances admit late compensation where single ones do not?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This census is one entrance at a time; the joint test needs (K_t c_i)_i in {(u c_i)_i : u in W_t} for every t.
open_questions.first_step: Run the joint test over pairs of disjoint supports in the same class V using the W_t spaces in RESULT.json.

open_questions.question: Does a different scatter enlarge W_t enough to admit a late single entrance?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The coordinate W_t of at most 5 helpers is a property of this scatter; added snapshot terms are already inside the class and change nothing.
open_questions.first_step: Move one retained total to another helper and recompute W_t.
open_questions.blocked_by: Pricing the changed COPY with #1128 section 5's argument.
